newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghanistan main security concern at C. Asian talks.
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan main security concern at C. Asian talks.

text.p: Foreign ministers from the former Soviet republics of Central Asia and Russia met in the Tajik capital, Dushanbe, on Saturday to discuss fears of more fighting in neighbouring Afghanistan.

The foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan and Russia's first deputy foreign minister, Boris Pastukhov, were present at the start of the talks, the Tajik Foreign Ministry's press centre said by telephone from Dushanbe.
The ministry added that a joint declaration was expected later on Saturday.

Kazakh Foreign Minister Kosymzhomart Tokayev told Reuters on the eve of his departure to Tajikistan on Friday: "We want to discuss the situation in the region and particularly the influence of Afghanistan."

Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov met the visiting ministers briefly on Saturday. A Tajik official cited Rakhmonov as saying that, if urgent measures were not taken, the situation in Afghanistan could spin out of control, undermining security not only in Central Asia but throughout the ex-Soviet states.

The official said Rakhmonov had called for the creation of an international forum to find a political solution to Afghanistan's long-running civil war, involving all factions and other interested countries.
The fall of the Afghan capital Kabul in September last year to the purist Islamic Taleban militia sent shock waves through the Central Asian republics.
Central Asian leaders are hostile to Islamic fundamentalism and fear Afghan chaos could spill over their common borders and undermine their own fragile stability.
They also fear a refugee crisis if the Taleban push northwards against rival factions in the spring.
The commander of one of Afghanistan's anti-Taleban factions, Ahmad Shah Masood, is already using a southern Tajik airport to send supplies to his forces inside the war-ravaged country.
Turkmenistan, which has declared itself a neutral country and which borders Afghanistan, did not send any representatives, saying they were busy elsewhere.
